arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argued that long-term residents with two minor drug convictions should not be categorically ineligible for relief.
The government argued that Congress intended all aliens engaging in the same serious conduct to be treated the same.
Justice Sotomayor questioned the elements of the recidivism finding and the underlying State statutes.
Justice Kennedy asked if the second unlawful entry makes the entry lawful.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of federal immigration law. It asks if a second minor drug conviction automatically bars a lawful permanent resident from seeking discretionary relief. the side that brought the case argues deep family ties should allow for relief. The government argues uniform treatment requires mandatory removal for all such offenders.
